title: Butter chicken
steps: Mix the chicken with all the marinade ingredients and leave for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Cook the chicken in a hot, lightly oiled pan or under a very hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. It does not need to be cooked through.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan. Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and cook for about 15 minutes until soft and jammy.
Blend the tomatoes until smooth and return the sauce to the pan.
Add the chicken and a splash of water if the sauce is thick. Simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the cream, crushed kasuri methi, sugar if using, and the remaining butter. Warm through for 2 minutes and adjust the salt.
Serve with naan or basmati rice.
notes: Use a small amount of chilli powder for mild heat; kashmiri chilli adds colour more than heat.

title: Masala dosa with potato filling
steps: Soak the rice, and separately the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds, in plenty of water for 5 to 6 hours.
Grind the dal to a fluffy, light batter, adding cold water a little at a time. Grind the rice more coarsely. Combine, add salt and mix well with your hand.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 8 to 12 hours until bubbly and slightly sour. The batter should roughly double.
For the filling, heat 2 tbsp oil. Add the mustard seeds, and when they pop add the curry leaves, chilli and onion. Cook until soft.
Add the turmeric, potatoes, salt and a splash of water. Mix and cook for 5 minutes, then keep warm.
Heat a flat non-stick or cast-iron pan until hot. Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and spiral it outward into a thin circle. Drizzle a little oil around the edge.
Cook until the underside is deep golden and the top is dry. Spoon the filling along the centre, fold and serve at once with coconut chutney and sambar.
notes: The first dosa usually tears. Wipe the pan with half an onion between dosas to stop sticking.

title: Hilsa in mustard sauce

ingredients.note: black or yellow, soaked in warm water 15 minutes and ground with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt

steps: Rub the fish with salt and half the turmeric and set aside for 10 minutes.
Grind the soaked mustard seeds with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste. Avoid over-grinding, which makes the paste bitter. Mix it with 150 ml cold water.
Heat the mustard oil until it just starts to smoke, then lower the heat. Add the fish and fry lightly for 1 to 2 minutes per side without browning.
Pour the mustard mixture over the fish, add the slit chillies and the remaining turmeric, and cover.
Cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring so the fish stays intact.
Finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil and serve with plain steamed rice.
notes: Hilsa has many fine bones. Frozen hilsa is available at South Asian grocers. Rohu or another oily fish can stand in.

title: Instant khaman dhokla
steps: Grease a 20 cm round tin and set up a steamer with boiling water.
Whisk the besan, yogurt, sugar, ginger, chilli, turmeric, lemon juice and salt with about 200 ml water into a smooth, pourable batter. Rest for 10 minutes.
Stir in the baking soda just before steaming. The batter will foam up.
Pour into the tin and steam, covered, for 15 to 18 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and curry leaves, and when they crackle pour in the sugar water and bring to a boil.
Cut the dhokla into squares, spoon the tempering over the top and leave 5 minutes to absorb. Serve with green chutney.

title: Gulab jamun with milk powder
steps: Boil the sugar, water and cardamom for 5 to 6 minutes until lightly sticky. Add the rose water and keep the syrup warm.
Mix the milk powder, flour and baking soda. Rub in the melted ghee, then add the warm milk a spoonful at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. Do not knead hard.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes, then roll into about 16 smooth, crack-free balls. They will double in size.
Heat the frying fat to a low medium heat, about 130 to 140 C. Fry the balls in batches, turning constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until deep golden brown all over.
Lift out, drain briefly and drop into the warm syrup.
Soak for at least 2 hours so they swell and absorb the syrup. Serve warm.
notes: If the fat is too hot the outside browns while the centre stays raw. Cracks in the balls mean the dough was too dry.
